summary: Tekken entries from Sami's spine and sourced supplemental seeds, built for per-platform route research.

entries.title: Tekken 8

emulation.notes: Use the native Windows PC release with current patches and known fixes/settings where needed.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Highest: native PC settings and capture flexibility.

primary.why: Windows PC is the highest-fidelity practical route among the available platforms, with strong support for PC-specific configuration and capture. Use the same patched season/content state across platforms; no platform-exclusive campaign content exists.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows PC release with current patches, native/high-resolution output, and known fixes or settings as needed; install owned story/content DLC before capture.

entries.remaster_caveats: No separate remaster split is promoted; use the current patched PC build and owned DLC/content.

entries.title: Tekken 3
entries.definitive_edition: PlayStation version for complete content; arcade for original competitive presentation

emulation.emulator: DuckStation for PlayStation; MAME for arcade comparison
emulation.notes: Use accurate settings and avoid visual hacks if comparing arcade versus home versions.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Accurate PlayStation emulation for complete route; MAME/arcade hardware for original route

primary.version: PlayStation version via DuckStation or original hardware
primary.why: The arcade original has the cleanest original graphics, but the PlayStation version adds substantial home content such as Tekken Force. For Sami's minimize-replays philosophy, the PlayStation version is the completeness-first main route.
primary.how_to_play: Use a legally owned PlayStation copy on original hardware or DuckStation with accurate settings. Use arcade/MAME only for comparison against the original arcade presentation.

secondary.what_to_play: Run a short comparison arcade set if the archive wants original arcade fidelity.
secondary.why: PlayStation is the complete route, but the arcade version is the original competitive presentation.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern standalone remaster is sourced for Tekken 3. Tekken 5 includes the arcade version, not the full PlayStation home package.

entries.title: Tekken 7
entries.definitive_edition: Tekken 7 Definitive Edition/current Steam PC build with all owned DLC

emulation.notes: Use native PC for the main route; arcade emulation or original hardware only for a branch comparison.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Native PC at final DLC-season state

primary.version: Steam Definitive Edition / final DLC-season state
primary.why: The PC release gives the cleanest capture route and, through the Definitive Edition/current Steam package, can include the large post-launch DLC roster and content set. The original arcade branch matters historically, but the home version is the completeness route.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Steam PC version with all owned DLC installed, ideally the Definitive Edition content set. Record game version, installed DLC/season content, controller, graphics settings, and whether any arcade/Fated Retribution comparison was captured.

secondary.exclusive_content: Original arcade and Fated Retribution branch presentation/balance
secondary.what_to_play: Run a short arcade/Fated Retribution comparison only if documenting the competitive arcade lineage.
secondary.why: The arcade release predates the home story/DLC package and is a historically distinct branch.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record DLC ownership and final patch state, since the roster/content set changed substantially after launch.

entries.title: Tekken 6
entries.definitive_edition: PS3/Xbox 360 home version based on Bloodline Rebellion

emulation.emulator: RPCS3/Xenia only if original hardware is unavailable
emulation.notes: Use original hardware for primary where possible; arcade emulation only for branch comparison.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PS3/Xbox 360 home version with final update

primary.version: Home version based on Bloodline Rebellion
primary.why: The PS3/Xbox 360 home versions are based on the Bloodline Rebellion update and add the main home content package, including Scenario Campaign context and online-era features. Arcade remains the competitive original route, while PSP is a portable adaptation.
primary.how_to_play: Use PS3 or Xbox 360 hardware with final title update if available. Record platform, patch, controller, roster/unlocks, Scenario Campaign progress, online shutdown/availability, and whether arcade Bloodline Rebellion was compared.

secondary.exclusive_content: Original arcade balance and branch history
secondary.what_to_play: Run a short comparison only if documenting the arcade lineage.
secondary.why: The arcade route predates the home package and has competitive-history value.
It is not the main fidelity route.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record patch, unlock state, Scenario Campaign progress, and online-service availability.

entries.title: Tekken 2
entries.definitive_edition: PlayStation version, with arcade comparison if original fidelity matters

emulation.emulator: DuckStation for PlayStation; MAME for arcade comparison
emulation.notes: Prefer original hardware or accurate settings; record BIOS/core and latency settings.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original arcade hardware for arcade fidelity; PlayStation hardware for home route

primary.version: PlayStation version via original hardware or accurate emulation
primary.why: Tekken 2 began in arcades, but the PlayStation version is the more complete one-route archive target because it adds home modes and unlockable content. The arcade version should be compared if original arcade presentation or competitive balance is the goal.
primary.how_to_play: Use a legally owned PlayStation copy on original hardware or DuckStation with accurate settings. Record region, emulator/core or hardware, controller, memory-card/unlock state, modes played, and whether arcade/MAME was compared.

secondary.what_to_play: Run an arcade comparison if documenting original competitive context.
secondary.why: The PlayStation route is more complete, but arcade is the original release.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record region, unlock state, and whether the arcade version was compared.

emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original arcade hardware for arcade fidelity; PlayStation hardware for home route

entries.title: Tekken 5
entries.definitive_edition: PlayStation 2 version, with Dark Resurrection separately if revision coverage matters

emulation.emulator: PCSX2 if original PS2 hardware is unavailable
emulation.notes: Record emulator version, BIOS, renderer, resolution, and latency settings.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original PlayStation 2 hardware for home route; arcade hardware for competitive route

primary.why: Tekken 5 began in arcades, but the PS2 version is the best one-route archive target because it includes home modes, Devil Within, customization, and arcade-history versions of earlier Tekken games. Dark Resurrection is an important follow-up revision and should be logged separately if played.
primary.how_to_play: Use the PS2 version on original hardware or PCSX2 with accurate settings. Record region, hardware/emulator, controller, unlock/customization state, Devil Within progress, Arcade History use, and whether arcade/Dark Resurrection was compared.

secondary.exclusive_content: Original arcade balance and later revision content
secondary.what_to_play: Use if documenting competitive arcade lineage or the Dark Resurrection revision.
secondary.why: The PS2 route is content-rich, but arcade revisions are historically distinct.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record unlocks, customization, region, Arcade History use, and whether Dark Resurrection was compared.

entries.title: Tekken Tag Tournament 2
entries.definitive_edition: Tekken Tag Tournament 2: Wii U Edition for content, with PS3/Xbox 360 or arcade comparison if needed

emulation.emulator: Cemu optional for Wii U comparison
emulation.notes: Use original Wii U hardware for the main route if input latency matters.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Wii U/PS3/Xbox 360 hardware depending on route; arcade hardware for arcade timing

primary.version: Tekken Tag Tournament 2: Wii U Edition
primary.why: There is no native PC version. The Wii U Edition is the most complete home route because it includes the base console game plus Nintendo-themed costumes, Mushroom Battle, and Tekken Ball-style extra content. PS3/Xbox 360 remain useful for base console comparison and online history.
primary.how_to_play: Use Wii U Edition on original hardware or a documented emulator setup. Record patch/DLC state, controller/stick, display latency, stage/music settings, Mushroom Battle/Tekken Ball coverage, online state, and whether PS3/Xbox 360 were compared.

secondary.exclusive_content: Original HD console ecosystem and competitive baseline
secondary.what_to_play: Use if documenting the non-Wii U console version or legacy online state.
secondary.why: Wii U is more complete for content; PS3/Xbox 360 are the main original home routes.
The home versions have additional content and practice modes.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern PC/remaster route. Record online/DLC status and controller latency.

entries.title: Tekken 4
entries.definitive_edition: PlayStation 2 release through hardware or PCSX2, with arcade comparison if timing matters

emulation.notes: Use original PS2 hardware when input latency matters; PCSX2 for high-resolution capture.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original PS2 hardware for home route; arcade hardware for arcade timing

primary.version: PlayStation 2 home release with arcade comparison
primary.why: Tekken 4 has no native PC version. The PS2 release is the complete home route with additional modes, while the arcade System 246 version remains the timing/reference route.
primary.how_to_play: Use an original PS2 copy or PCSX2 with owned media. Record emulator version, renderer, internal resolution, input latency, controller/stick, Tekken Force/Story/Practice coverage, and whether arcade hardware behavior was compared.

secondary.what_to_play: Use if validating arcade rules, timing, or balance.
secondary.why: PS2 is the fuller home package, but arcade is the original release.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record emulator upscaling and latency; no modern PC/remaster route exists.

entries.title: Tekken Tag Tournament
entries.definitive_edition: Tekken Tag Tournament HD in Tekken Hybrid; arcade route for strict origin timing

emulation.notes: Use PS3 for HD route; arcade emulation only for strict comparison.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Official HD route or original arcade timing with route documented

primary.version: Tekken Tag Tournament HD via Tekken Hybrid
primary.why: The arcade version is the original tag-fighting route, but Tekken Tag Tournament HD in Tekken Hybrid is the cleanest official high-fidelity home route. The PS2 version remains important as a launch-title/home-content route with Tekken Bowl.
primary.how_to_play: Use Tekken Hybrid on PS3 for the HD route, or original arcade/PS2 for strict history. Record route, controller/stick, character/team, mode, unlocks, Tekken Bowl state, display settings, and whether arcade timing was compared.

secondary.exclusive_content: Original arcade timing and PS2 launch-title home content
secondary.why: Tekken Hybrid is the current cleaner HD route but not the arcade original.
